result.title: Benchmarking CNNs, Vision Transformers, and Foundation Models for Explainable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: Calibration, Decision Analysis, and External Validation
result.comment: Under review at Scientific Report Journal, Springer
result.summary: Deep learning models for brain tumor MRI classification are usually compared by accuracy alone, on public datasets whose independence is rarely checked. We benchmarked six architectures: two convolutional networks (EfficientNetV2-M and ConvNeXt-V2-Tiny), two vision transformers (Swin-V2-S and ViT-L/16), and two foundation models (DINOv2-L and MedSigLIP-448), for four-class classification of 7,216 public MRI images. We assessed accuracy, calibration, explainability, ensembles, and decision curves, with every fitted quantity estimated on validation data only. Pixel-verified duplicate screening showed that 36% of the test images had a near-duplicate in the training data. Test accuracy ranged from 94.5% to 95.6%, with no pairwise difference after Holm correction, and fell to 90.3% to 91.7% on the 773 test images free of duplicates and shared patients. Ensembles did not outperform the best single model. Attribution maps passed a model-randomization test but localized expert-annotated tumors poorly. On 1,675 external BDNeuro-MRI images that did not duplicate the training data, accuracy ranged from 77.6% (MedSigLIP-448) to 95.0% (ViT-L/16), and 12 of 15 pairwise differences were significant. Internal accuracy on this public collection therefore did not distinguish the architectures, whereas the duplicate-filtered external test did.

AI.brief_summary: 在 7,216 张脑肿瘤 MRI 上将六种 CNN、ViT 与基础模型做四分类基准，比较准确率、校准、可解释性、集成与决策曲线，并做去重筛查与 1,675 张外部图像验证；发现内部准确率无法区分架构，且归因图虽通过模型随机化检验却定位专家标注肿瘤较差。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文本身是医学分类基准而非推理研究，但其归因图的模型随机化检验与定位评估，可能为核查 LVR 中视觉证据是否真正被内部状态使用、以及旁路虚假利用提供可借鉴的检验线索，需进一步核查迁移可行性。
